checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] a body whose strip has been edited elsewhere is refused
checks._why: This edit is six lines matched as one string. The day someone touches any of them, the pattern stops matching, and without this refusal the program writes a sheet whose Body HTML is the live body unchanged. Matrixify imports it, logs a success, and the page is exactly as it was. A silent no-op on a body edit is indistinguishable from a working run.

checks.name: the day values must survive in unitDays(), because 37 days of pacing hang off them
checks.find: if (!after.includes('u.' + f)) problems.push(f + ' no longer feeds unitDays(), which would move every day number');
checks.expect_failure: [FAIL] removing the data from unitDays() is refused
checks._why: unitDays() sums frqDays, labDays and testDays into each unit's span, and the running day numbers down the whole page are built from it. Taking the values out along with their display would move 37 days of pacing that a teacher may already be planning against, and nothing on the page would say so.

_hollow_guard_removed: A fifth mutation targeted a 'nothing outside the strip moved' check in repair(). It survived: the suite stayed green with the guard broken, because a single replace(BEFORE, AFTER) with more-than-one already refused cannot change anything outside the strip. The guard was unfalsifiable, so it was deleted rather than decorated. The property is still asserted against the real body in the suite. This note exists so the next reader does not add it back believing it was an oversight.
